end.summary:
Defined food miles as the distance food travels from source to home.
Linked greater distance with more fuel use and pollution.
Identified local food as travelling a shorter distance and discussed freshness.
Located mangoes on trees and carrots in fields; teach-back was not passed.
end.parentNote: Rohan practised defining food miles, tracing where foods come from, and comparing local and distant food. They used the method of connecting distance with truck or ship fuel, and later explained that shorter travel can help food arrive sooner and stay fresher. They initially hesitated about where mangoes and carrots grow, then gave the correct locations; this was corrected later in the lesson (correctAfterLastSeen). At home, ask Rohan to choose two foods and write where each grows, how far it may travel, and one effect of that distance.
